question.text: Lakshmi is reviewing the reporting frequency of a Category I/II AIF during DD. Which reporting standard reflects the workbook's source-backed timelines?

answer.text: Annual report only, shared at the fund's AGM
No formal reporting — investors can call the fund manager anytime

Valuation at least once every six months (extendable to annual with 75% investor approval), annual financial information within 180 days of year-end, and periodic portfolio/risk/operational/transactional disclosures per fund documents
Monthly WhatsApp messages from the fund manager

explanation.text: The Logic: For Category I/II AIFs, the workbook specifies valuation at least once every six months (extendable to annual with approval of 75% of investors by value), disclosure of financial information within 180 days from year-end (or earlier per fund documents), and periodic disclosure of financial, risk, operational, portfolio, and transactional information. The Trap: Annual-only reporting is insufficient. Informal channels lack documentation. Quarterly NAV disclosure is associated with Category III close-ended AIFs in the timeline table, not Category I/II. Note: Based on workbook pages 205, 206, 210, 212, and 214 covering Category I/II investor reporting.
